resources.string: Messages hop from phone to phone — no internet needed. Say hello in Nearby to reach everyone in range, or add a contact to message one person directly.
Call your contacts, nearby or far away, and send short videos in any chat.

Near you, a call runs over a direct Wi-Fi link between the two phones, with no Internet needed. Farther away, it goes over the Internet while an internet relay is switched on. Only the two of you can hear it.

When there\'s no other way through, Knit places a mesh call instead. Hold the button to talk, and your voice reaches the other phone in short bursts, about a second behind you between neighbours. Nothing is saved to the chat, and you can start a mesh call yourself from a contact\'s profile.
Send a video in any chat, Nearby included. Knit shrinks it to about 3 MB and keeps up to 61 seconds. A video only Bluetooth can bring waits for your tap.

Supporting Knit on Ko-fi or GitHub Sponsors comes with Knit Anywhere, which lets your internet relay carry your calls, photos and files to people no phone nearby can reach. Open the invite link you\'re sent to add it.
Turn on Low-power mode in Settings to switch Wi-Fi Aware off and save battery. It also comes on by itself with Battery Saver. Messages still arrive over Bluetooth, but photos and files take longer.
Farther Bluetooth, and progress on incoming photos
Phones connect from farther apart, and incoming photos show their progress.

Phones now find each other over Bluetooth from farther apart. Near the edge of range, a connection switches to Bluetooth\'s long-range mode to stay up. Both phones need that mode, so iPhones and phones without it connect as before.
Photos, voice messages and files from a nearby phone show a ring that fills as they arrive, so you can tell slow from stuck.

Set this board up for Knit?

This adds the Knit channel to your board and changes a few of its settings: it renames the board “Knit” so you can pick it out on the mesh, stops broadcasting its position and node info, and stops relaying other radios' traffic to save battery.

It also marks the board “unmonitored”. Knit only reads Knit's own messages, so an ordinary Meshtastic message sent to this board would never reach you — the mark tells other people's apps that, instead of letting them write to a board nobody is reading.

Your board's own main channel is left alone and it stays on the public Meshtastic frequency, so other radios can still pass your messages along.

This room shows the primary channel of the Meshtastic radio paired to this phone. Knit\'s encryption does not reach it: nothing here is end-to-end encrypted, and on the standard Meshtastic channel the key is public, so anyone with a radio can read it. Anyone with a radio in range can post and anyone can claim any name, so treat both as unverified, even a name that matches one of your contacts. The one exception is a contact\'s name with a shield beside it: their radio signed that post, and the signature checked out against the radio their profile names. A matching name without the shield is still a guess. Some posts arrive from the Internet rather than from anyone nearby.
